ideas.name: BlockVouch
ideas.problem: The erosion of trust in global review platforms caused by bot accounts, fake ratings, and the lack of localized, neighbor-vetted accountability for home services.
ideas.targetUser: Homeowners and property managers aged 30-55 living in high-density residential areas who prioritize reliability and community proximity over the lowest price.
coreFeatures: The 'Neighbor Vouch': A verified-resident-only recommendation system that requires proof of proximity to issue a vouch.
Proof-of-Work Ledger: A visual feed of service completion photos and receipts attached to specific vouches to validate the claim.
Proximity Heatmap: An interactive map showing recent, verified service activity within a 5-block radius of the user.
Micro-Community Verification: An address-validation gatekeeper that ensures reviewers are actual neighbors, not random internet users.
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform (Geocoding and Places API)
Stripe Identity (KYC for address verification)
AWS S3 (Evidence image hosting)
Firebase Authentication (User management)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'mock_data.json' containing 50 simulated 'Vouches' with hardcoded GPS coordinates clustered around a single neighborhood. Instead of a live Google Maps API, the app will render a high-resolution static map image with overlaid SVG markers for proximity. All 'Address Verification' steps will trigger a 4-second 'Verifying with Local Records...' loading state before returning a hardcoded 'Verified' status. Image uploads will be intercepted by a local handler that simulates a 2-second latency before displaying a local placeholder image, mimicking an S3 upload/download cycle.

ideas.name: NectarNet
ideas.problem: The creation of seasonal 'nectar deserts' caused by uncoordinated residential gardening, which creates gaps in food availability for local pollinators.
ideas.targetUser: Environmentally conscious residential gardeners, suburban neighborhood associations, and community garden coordinators looking to build wildlife corridors.
coreFeatures: Neighborhood Bloom Timeline: A shared, localized calendar visualizing current and upcoming flowering windows on a per-street basis.
Nectar Gap Forecaster: An automated detection engine that identifies upcoming weeks where local floral coverage will drop below a sustainable threshold.
Sync-Planting Matchmaker: A recommendation engine that suggests specific plant species to a user based on the 'gaps' identified by their neighbors.
Corridor Connectivity Score: A community-wide gamified metric that tracks the total number of consecutive blooming days achieved by the neighborhood.
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform (Maps SDK and Geocoding API)
Perenual or Trefle Plant API (botanical and blooming cycle data)
Firebase Cloud Messaging (for localized gap-alert notifications)
PostGIS (for spatial queries regarding proximity and neighborhood boundaries)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'mock_data.json' file containing a curated set of 15 neighborhood users, each with fixed lat/long coordinates and a 'garden' array of plant objects. The Plant API will be replaced by an asynchronous function that returns these plant objects with a randomized delay (500ms to 1800ms) to simulate network latency. Instead of real-time GPS, the app will default to a hardcoded 'Neighborhood Center' coordinate. To demonstrate the Gap Forecaster, a 'Season Slider' UI component will be implemented, allowing the developer to manually advance the app's internal system clock through Spring, Summer, and Fall, triggering the gap-detection logic based on the hardcoded bloom dates in the mock data.

ideas.name: Stoop
ideas.problem: The 'Planning Friction' gap where neighbors chat about gathering but fail to execute due to the high cognitive load of coordinating food, timing, and attendance in unorganized group chats.
ideas.targetUser: Urban apartment dwellers and suburban neighbors (ages 25-45) who desire low-stakes, spontaneous social interaction without the social pressure or logistics of a formal hosted event.
coreFeatures: One-Tap 'Flash-Host' Templates (e.g., 'Sidewalk Sundaes', 'Porch Toast', 'Driveway Coffee')
Micro-Potluck Grid (Visual, low-friction sign-up for hyper-specific small items like 'Ice', 'Napkins', or 'One Bag of Chips')
Proximity-Verified Guest Lists (Automatic filtering of users within a 500m radius to ensure hyper-local relevance)
The 'Vibe' Check (Ultra-fast binary voting for quick consensus on event time or theme)
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform (Geofencing and location-based discovery)
Supabase Realtime (Live RSVP and potluck list synchronization)
Twilio API (SMS-based hyper-local notifications)
Cloudinary (Image hosting for event aesthetic snapshots)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a 'MockProvider' wrapper for all service calls, returning Promises that resolve after a randomized delay of 400ms to 1200ms to simulate real network latency. A static 'Neighborhood State' JSON file will act as the database, pre-populating the app with mock users, events, and potluck items. Proximity logic will be emulated through a 'Simulated Location' toggle in the settings, which switches the user's coordinates between pre-defined 'Neighborhood Zones' to trigger the visibility of different mock events.

ideas.name: LobbyLink
ideas.niche: Hyperlocal residential package and key coordination
ideas.problem: Package theft ('porch piracy') in communal lobbies and the lack of a trusted, real-time communication system for neighbors to secure items for one another in buildings without concierges.
ideas.targetUser: Urban professionals and frequent online shoppers aged 25-45 living in high-density apartment complexes or managed buildings that lack 24/7 onsite staff.
coreFeatures: Verified Neighbor Circles (Building-specific authentication via invite code)
Secure QR Hand-off (One-time scan protocol to confirm successful item transfer)
Real-time Hand-off Status (Live tracking: 'In Lobby' to 'With Neighbor' to 'Collected')
Photo-Proof Verification (Mandatory photo upload of item location or recipient hand-off)
realDependencies: Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) for real-time push notifications
Google Maps Geolocation API for proximity-based building verification
AWS S3 for secure storage of hand-off verification photos
Stripe Identity or manual admin dashboard for tenant vetting
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local JSON state machine to mimic a database of neighbors and package statuses. Geolocation will be simulated by a 'Mock Location' toggle that bypasses GPS checks. Push notifications will be emulated using in-app 'Toast' UI components triggered by a timer to mimic incoming alerts. QR scanning will be replaced by a 'Simulate Scan' button that invokes a 1.5-second loading spinner to mimic camera processing and server validation. All image uploads will use a scripted progress bar that resolves to a dummy URL after 2 seconds.

ideas.name: GatherGo
ideas.niche: Hyperlocal peer-to-peer micro-rentals for short-duration event supplies.
ideas.problem: The 'Small-Scale Event Gap': Professional rental services are too costly and inconvenient for minor needs (1-2 hours/days), while community forums lack the infrastructure for secure, transactional borrowing.
ideas.targetUser: Suburban homeowners (ages 25-50) hosting backyard gatherings; budget-conscious DIY event planners; and neighborhood 'super-providers' who own surplus party supplies.
coreFeatures: Hyperlocal Radius Search (Map-based proximity discovery)
Micro-Slot Booking (Hourly and daily availability toggles)
Secure Escrow Payments & Instant Deposits
Peer-to-Peer Chat & Item Handover Checklists
Neighbor Trust Score & Identity Verification
realDependencies: Stripe API (Payment Processing & Escrow)
Google Maps Platform (Geo-location & Routing)
Firebase (Real-time Database & Authentication)
Twilio (SMS Notifications)
Cloudinary (Image Management for gear listings)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The prototype will utilize a local JSON 'World State' to simulate the backend. The Map will be a Leaflet.js instance with pre-defined coordinate points representing 'items' in a specific neighborhood. Payment flows will trigger a 2-second CSS loading spinner followed by a hardcoded 'Success' or 'Declined' boolean response. Chat will use a `setTimeout` loop to inject messages from a 'Neighbor' persona into the UI to simulate real-time interaction. All geolocation will be relative to a fixed central coordinate to ensure consistent demo results without requiring real GPS movement.
